sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4.86 billion in FY2016 to $14.3 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was two regimes rather than one trend.
FY2021 was the step change: revenue rose 89.1% to $16.1 billion [F6][D241], with REGEN-COV contributing 66.4pp and US net product sales 77.1pp of that growth [D582][D471].
The FY2022 reversal took revenue down 24.3% to $12.2 billion [F7][D292], as REGEN-COV sales fell to zero after new SARS-CoV-2 variants proved not susceptible to the treatment [S49][P7].
Since then revenue has grown only 5.6% a year over FY2022..FY2025 [D767], and operating income has compounded at -8.9% over the same span [D769].
In FY2025 collaboration revenue of $7.33 billion was 51.1% of revenue and contributed 9.0pp of growth [S22][D521][D523], while net product sales fell 17.3% and subtracted 9.3pp [D506][D507].

US EYLEA net product sales fell 42.4% to $2.75 billion [S43][D577], which the filing attributes to lower volumes from competitive pressure, share loss to compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition, plus a lower net selling price [P10].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits rose 33.6% and added 9.3pp [D591][D592], driven by higher Dupixent sales [P9].
Operating costs grew 4.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025 [D464], at 5.4% [D457], so incremental margin was negative and operating income fell 10.3% against 1.0% revenue growth [D441][D440].
Diluted EPS grew 8.2% against 2.1% net income growth [D444][D442] as the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% is the window low, below the 34.6% median and far below the 55.7% FY2021 high [F30][D749][D751][D750].
R&D took 4.7pp off the margin and SG&A added 2.0pp back, leaving the 3.2pp decline [D465][D466][D453].
The SG&A relief came from lower charitable contributions to Good Days, partly offset by about $60 million of fourth-quarter matching donations [P5].
In FY2025 net margin of 31.4% sat 6.5pp above the 24.9% operating margin [F50][F30], as other income of $1.65 billion [X117] and a 13.9% tax rate [D427] lifted the bottom line.

FY2025 operating cash flow of $4.98 billion was 1.11x net income [F80][D428], and free cash flow of $4.08 billion was 0.91x net income [F100][D429], above the 0.88x free-cash-flow window median [D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% sits above the 26.4% window median [D425][D757] and well above the 22.0% peer median [D777].
Capex of $898 million was 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [F90][D424][D430], reflecting the multi-year build-out the filings describe [P19].
Stock-based compensation of $994 million absorbed 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431].
Net cash of $16.9 billion is 117.7% of revenue [D434][D435], in the 100th percentile of the eight-peer group against a -50.7% median [D780][D781].
Cash and investments rose 5.3% to $18.9 billion [D432][D460] against total debt of $1.99 billion [D433], and the current ratio is 4.13x [F180].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.81 billion were 93.3% of free cash flow [D436][D437], including a first $370 million dividend [X140], and the share count fell 5.6% [D459].
Return on average equity of 14.9% is in the 25th percentile against a 38.7% peer median [D439][D784][D785].
Operating margin has fallen four years running, from 55.7% in FY2021 to 24.9% in FY2025, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1].

The compression is now structural rather than cyclical: EYLEA's US franchise is shrinking [S43] while R&D runs at 40.8% of revenue [D420], so the margin has little room to recover without a new growth driver.
FY2018 and FY2019 revenue in the table are later recasts, $5.15 billion and $6.56 billion against $6.71 billion and $7.86 billion as first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2018 revenue decline of 12.4% [D92] should not be read as an operating event.
Whether US EYLEA net product sales fall further from $2.75 billion in FY2025 [S43], which would extend the product-sales decline, in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether the operating margin holds at or above the 24.9% FY2025 window low [F30][D749], in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether R&D as a share of revenue stays at or above the 40.8% FY2025 level [D420], against the 34.6% window median [D760], in the FY2026 10-K.
